newsitem.title: UK: U.K. welcomes new offshore oil safety guidelines.
newsitem.headline: U.K. welcomes new offshore oil safety guidelines.

text.p: The U.K. Health and Safety Executive (HSE) has reacted warmly to stricter guidelines for rescue and recovery arrangements at offshore oil and gas installations on the U.K. continental shelf.

"The HSE and the MSA (Marine Safety Agency) welcome the new guidelines as they take account of new technology in the rescue and recovery arena and set new standards over and above those previously established," an HSE statement said.
The new guidelines, which will be in effect on November 1, will replace what is currently known as the Green Code - a set of instructions from the Department of Transport.
"The U.K. offshore oil and gas industry has given a commitment that to employ only vessels which meet these standards."
Jeremy Daniel, chairman of the Standby Ship Operators' Association (SSOA), said a key element in the guidelines was the time taken to rescue people from the sea.

"These industry guidelines raise standards, but in a way which will allow further improvements in equipment, technique and knowledge to be brought into operation much more simply and quickly than before," he said in a statement.

No details were given of the new guidelines, which were issued jointly by a collection of offshore industry players and follow government recommendations that responsibility for offshore safety should be handed over from the government to industry.
